key_insight: Seer strengthens small deep-research agents by using shared models to predict and score candidate actions before executing only the selected action.
engineering_relevance: Reusable offline-trained guidance supports locally run agents without per-agent retraining or real tool calls for discarded candidates, at the cost of extra inference.
method: Train a tool-response simulator on real research call–response pairs.
Train a value estimator on histories labeled with discounted terminal correctness.
Predict and score candidate outcomes, execute the selected action, and commit only real tool responses to history.
evidence_signal: Across multiple deep-research benchmarks, Seer improves different agents; GAIA accuracy rises from 13.6% to 41.7% for Qwen3.5-4B and from 22.3% to 50.5% for Qwen3.5-9B.
watch_item: Prediction and scoring errors limit gains from broader imagined search, while extra inference remains a deployment cost.
paper_title: Seer: Guiding Small Deep-Research Agents with Shared Decision Models
